name: DeepSearchQA skill tuning for MiniMax M3 (you-web)

description: baseline: current pre-sync skill on seed-42 shard (no code change)

asi.hypothesis: baseline measurement of the current pre-sync skill (no code change) to anchor keep/discard
asi.iter1_plan: mechanical signature-sync: include_domains->site:cdc.gov (2x), drop offset, extraction_mode->extraction
asi.noise_observed: 0.047 spread between two baseline runs on the same 15-trial shard (0.8778 manual vs 0.8308 loop) = M3 generation variance; keep/discard must beat this to be meaningful
asi.shard: 5 tasks x k=3 = 15 trials, seed 42, 3 Single + 2 Set Answer
asi.tool_surface_lever: 13.2 calls/trial already < production 28.6; over-calling lever is small on this shard, headroom is correctness not call-count

description: iter 1: mechanical you-search signature sync (include_domains->site:, drop offset, extraction_mode->extraction). Within-noise drop; correctness baseline.

asi.behavior_change_note: the one real behavior change: site: operator now filters (include_domains was zod-stripped before, so site: was broken). This is the intended correctness fix. On the FAO task (#283, 'according to the FAO') the model may now narrow to site:fao.org — could help or over-narrow. Net effect on 5-task shard is small/noise.
asi.hypothesis: mechanical signature-sync: align skill param names to the current you-search surface (site: operator, drop offset, extraction enum). Behavior-neutral correctness baseline.
asi.next_action_hint: proceed to behavioral tuning: tool-call budget discipline + Set-Answer list discipline. If next 2 runs trend <0.80, investigate whether site: over-narrowing hurt the FAO task and soften the site: guidance.
asi.noise_context: drop 0.033 is within the 0.047 noise floor (2 baseline runs: 0.8778 manual, 0.8308 loop). sync is behavior-neutral by construction; keeping as the new correctness baseline per the approved iter-1 plan.

description: iter-2: tighter Phase 4 + tool budget — checks_failed on probe/ scratch env (fixed); metric equal-to-baseline on saturated shard

asi.env_fix: checks.sh now scopes tsc to .auto/tsconfig.checks.json (tracked src only); probe/ scratch excluded. Future runs won't stall on it.
asi.failure_diagnosis: shard is near-saturated: 4/5 tasks at 1.0. Leaks are stochastic: (a) deepsearchqa-115 trial2 = 3/3 correct but 7 EXCESSIVE authors -> F1 0.462 (answer-discipline leak); (b) deepsearchqa-762 trial0 = 0/1 correct, excluded France on bad urban-pop reasoning (search/correctness miss). The answer-discipline change targets (a) but the shard can't distinguish it from baseline (noise).
asi.hypothesis: iter-2: tighten Phase 4 answer discipline (exact set, no extras) + concrete tool budget (stop-when-found, 8-call ceiling).
asi.next_action: SWITCH eval shard to moderate-difficulty [0.3,0.7] tasks (239 available) for real headroom; re-baseline; re-apply answer-discipline there where Set-Answer excessive leaks are measurable. Holdout (50 tasks, 28 Set) remains the generalization truth-check.
asi.rollback_reason: checks failed on untracked probe/ scratch (tsc scanned gitignored files); env now fixed. Metric 0.8308 was equal-to-baseline on a near-saturated 5-task shard (4/5 at 1.0) = noise, not signal.

name: DeepSearchQA skill tuning for MiniMax M3 (hard headroom shard)

description: baseline (v2): synced skill on hard headroom shard — 5 tasks, 2 Single + 3 Set

asi.baseline_shard: hard shard v2 (seed 7): 5 tasks, 2 Single + 3 Set, prod 0.33-0.56
asi.failure_breakdown: 5/15 failures: 3 excessive-answer leaks (476 idx0/idx1 added Princeton +2; 525 idx1 added 7 extra countries, 5/5 correct but F1 0.588), 2 timeouts/failures (446 idx2 timed_out, 476 idx2 failed). 2 Single tasks (12, 804) saturated at 1.0.
asi.hypothesis: baseline of synced skill on hard shard — no code change
asi.key_lever: excessive answers on Set Answer (3/5 failures) + tool-call timeouts (2/15). Answer-discipline (no extras) + tool-budget (stop-when-found, fewer calls) directly target both.

description: iter1-v2: Phase 4 answer discipline (no extras) + concrete tool budget — +15.7% F1 (excessive leaks killed)

asi.delta: +0.1205 (+15.7%) vs baseline 0.7696 — well above 0.047 noise floor
asi.hypothesis: Phase 4 answer discipline (exact set, no extras, no padding) + concrete tool budget. Targets the 3 excessive-answer leaks + 2 timeouts observed in baseline.
asi.mechanism_note: F1 win is from answer discipline (reduced excessive answers). Tool budget '8 calls' was IGNORED — calls went UP 13.5->18. The model searches more to get the right set, which helped F1 but raised cost. Next: either enforce the budget harder or accept the higher calls if F1 keeps winning.
asi.next_action: Inspect per-task to confirm win = reduced excessive answers (not a fluke). Then either tighten Set-Answer list format or reduce the timeout failures (2/15 in baseline). Watch tool_calls as a cost signal.
asi.secondary_note: tool_calls_per_trial 13.47->18.0 (+34%) is a cost regression but F1 is the primary; secondary rarely decides. The 8-call ceiling wording is not being followed by M3.

description: iter2-v2: Output Format filtered-answer-list — regressed -6% vs best (over-corrected recall or noise)

asi.delta: -0.057 vs best 0.8901 (iter1-v2); +0.064 vs baseline 0.77. Within ~1.2x noise floor — borderline.
asi.hypothesis: Output Format: force ## Answer to be a clean filtered list (only items matching criteria), relegate non-matching to ## Evidence. Target the 525 idx2 excessive leak (16 extra countries).
asi.next_action: Discard (regression). Re-run iter1-v2 state to confirm the 0.89 best is stable (2nd data point), then target a DIFFERENT lever: either 525 excessive via a more surgical fix, or 476 over-searching (42-46 calls, misses Harvard). Output Format filtering over-corrected or was noise.
asi.rollback_reason: worse than current best (0.8901->0.8333); Output Format change added verbosity without a clear F1 win. Simpler is better — revert.

description: iter3-v2: Phase 4 filter-candidates bullet — regressed -8% (active filtering hurts recall; 2/2 filter attempts failed)

asi.hypothesis: Phase 4 bullet 4: 'filter candidates to only matching items; ## Answer is the filtered set'. Target 525 idx2 excessive (16 extra).
asi.learning: ACTIVE filtering instructions hurt (2/2 attempts regressed: Output Format -0.057, Phase4 bullet -0.071). The model over-filters and drops CORRECT items (recall loss) > the precision gain. iter1-v2's simple 'no extra items' PROHIBITION is the right level — do not add active filtering.
asi.next_action: Revert to iter1-v2 (best). Re-run iter1-v2 to get a 2nd data point — if ~0.89 the filtering changes are real regressions and iter1-v2 is the stable best; if ~0.83 the 0.89 was noise and reconsider. Then target 476 over-searching (42-46 calls, misses Harvard) via a convergence rule, NOT filtering.
asi.rollback_reason: worse than best; active-filtering hurts recall (2/2 filter attempts regressed). Revert to the 'no extras' prohibition level.

description: confirm: iter1-v2 re-run = 0.9370 (2nd data point; mean ~0.91 vs baseline 0.77). Improvement solidly real.

asi.iter1_v2_runs: 0.8901, 0.9370 (mean ~0.91) — both well above baseline 0.77. 0.89 was not a fluke; +0.12-0.17 improvement is real.
asi.noise_floor_confirmed: 2-run spread 0.047; iter1-v2 mean ~0.91 vs baseline 0.77 = +0.14 (3.8x+ noise).
asi.note: no code change — confirmation run of the committed iter1-v2 skill. M3 generation variance landed higher this run (0.937 vs 0.890).
asi.validated_best: iter1-v2 (Phase 4 'no extras' prohibition + concrete tool budget) is the stable best. Active filtering HURTS (2/2 attempts regressed). Next lever: 476 over-searching/convergence (42-46 calls, misses Harvard) — NOT filtering.

description: iter4-v2: set-enumeration convergence rule — regressed -12% (per-member search is necessary; forcing 1-search loses recall)

asi.delta: -0.12 vs best mean 0.91; ~baseline. ~2.5x noise (likely real regression).
asi.hypothesis: Phase 2 bullet 6: set-enumeration efficiency (1 set search + 1 read, not per-member). Target the 476 42-call over-search + 11% holdout timeouts.
asi.learning: Convergence/efficiency rules HURT, like filtering. Set-enumeration tasks (476: 8 Ivy League unis) REQUIRE per-member searches — the authoritative page doesn't have all members in one place. Forcing '1 set search + 1 read' loses recall. 3 efficiency/filtering attempts all regressed. The model's verbose per-member enumeration is NECESSARY; the timeout tail (11%) is its structural cost, not fixable via skill text without recall loss.
asi.next_action: Discard. Try structurally-different lever: prevent 0-score TIMEOUTS via partial-answer-on-exhaustion (doesn't filter or reduce calls). Shard can't measure timeout benefit (no timeouts there) but can detect premature-give-up harm. Validate timeout benefit on a faster holdout if shard holds.
asi.rollback_reason: worse than best; forcing set-enumeration efficiency loses recall. 3rd efficiency/filtering attempt to regress.

description: iter5-v2: partial-answer + realistic tool budget — regressed -11% (calls and F1 coupled: 10 calls -> 0.80 vs 17 calls -> 0.91)

asi.calls_vs_f1: COUPLED. iter5: 10.27 calls -> 0.80 F1. iter1-v2: 17 calls -> 0.91 F1. Fewer calls = lower F1 (less thorough). The model needs ~17 calls for set-enumeration tasks; reducing them loses recall.
asi.hypothesis: Revise Tool Budget: remove unrealistic '8 ceiling', add 'per-member is fine, stop when checked' + 'partial > nothing, never time out'. Target 11% holdout timeout tail.
asi.key_insight: iter1-v2's '8 ceiling' was a LUCKILY-IGNORED ceiling (model did 17 calls = thorough = 0.91). The new wording made the model FOLLOW the budget (10 calls) -> less thorough -> 0.80. So the timeout tail is structural cost of necessary enumeration; NOT fixable by reducing calls (costs F1) or filtering (costs recall). Only adapter-timeout increase (off-limits) or smarter search would help.
asi.next_action: Discard. iter1-v2 is CONVERGED: 4 attempts to beat it (2 filtering, 1 convergence, 1 fewer-calls) ALL regressed. Record iter1-v2 as the final tuned skill. Present to user with holdout validation (completed-trial 0.787 > production 0.7317; 11% timeout tail is a known structural limitation).
asi.rollback_reason: worse than best; reducing calls costs F1 (calls and F1 coupled). iter1-v2's ignored-ceiling (17 calls) is the sweet spot.

description: iter6: softer Phase 4 anti-padding (no over-search pressure) — shard +0.078, PROVISIONAL pending holdout validation

asi.hypothesis: Softer Phase 4 anti-padding: 'include only items the question asks for; keep supporting context in evidence not answer list'. iter1-v2 was right on DIRECTION (excessive answers leak precision) but too INTENSE ('exact set/no omissions/grader scores only requested set' caused over-search -> 5 holdout timeouts). This drops the over-search pressure, keeps the anti-pad nudge.
asi.next_action: MUST holdout-validate before considering settled. Run .auto/holdout.sh on this skill; compare to synced reference (all-trial 0.7306, completed-trial 0.7884, 3 timeouts, 20.21 calls). If holdout completed-trial > 0.7884 AND all-trial >= 0.7306 (no extra timeouts), it's a real generalizable win -> keep. If tied/worse, revert to synced (commit 328137c).
asi.provisional: SHARD WIN +0.078 but UNVALIDATED. iter1-v2 was +0.14 on shard yet TIED on holdout. Do NOT treat as final until holdout confirms.
asi.shard_overfits: proven by iter1-v2: +0.14 shard, 0.788 vs 0.788 holdout completed-trial (tied), worse all-trial (5 extra timeouts).

description: iter6 holdout validation: softer Phase 4 REJECTED — completed-trial 0.748 < synced 0.788 (5th anti-pad variant to fail); reverted to synced

asi.decision: REVERTED to synced (commit b16dc18). iter6 was committed provisionally (shard +0.078) but the holdout rejected it — this log records the holdout validation.
asi.holdout_comparison: iter6 softer-Phase4 on SAME 50 holdout tasks: completed-trial F1 0.7479 (145 completed, 0 timeouts) vs synced 0.7884 (139 completed, 3 timeouts). completed-trial -0.04 (worse), all-trial 0.7229 vs 0.7306 (worse), pass 66.7% vs 71.3% (worse). 0 timeouts is nice but each completed answer is WORSE — not a win.
asi.hypothesis: Softer Phase 4 anti-padding (drop the over-search pressure from iter1-v2, keep the 'don't pad' nuge). Tested whether iter1-v2 was right on direction but too intense.
asi.learning: 5th anti-pad/filtering variant that fails to generalize (iter1-v2, iter2-v2 Output Format, iter3-v2 filter-candidates, iter6 softer). CONCLUSIVE: ANY skill-text instruction that tells the model to restrict/trim the answer list HURTS completed-trial recall on the real distribution. The model over-filters and drops correct items. The excessive-answer 'leak' visible on the 5-task shard is NOT fixable via skill text without recall loss. The grader's excessive-answer penalty is real but the cure (filtering) is worse than the disease.
asi.next_action: Skill-text answer-discipline is a DEAD END (5/5 failed to generalize). Stop pursuing Phase 4 / Output Format / filtering variants. The remaining generalizable levers are NOT skill-text: (1) raise adapter timeout (off-limits src/) to kill the timeout tail, (2) a larger eval shard so the loop's metric is trustworthy. Recommend stopping the skill-tuning loop — the synced skill (signature sync) is the honest best, and further shard iterations will keep overfitting.
asi.rollback_reason: holdout rejected: completed-trial F1 0.748 < synced 0.788 (real regression, above noise). Softer anti-pad still costs recall.

description: iter7: Phase 4 answer-faithfulness (no hedge, no contradict) — shard +0.107, PROVISIONAL pending holdout (3rd shard-win, both prior rejected)

asi.diagnosis_source: Diagnosed from PRODUCTION graded.jsonl (898 tasks) to keep holdout clean as validation set — zero-correct completed failures are heterogeneous: counting errors, hedging ('most likely'), contradicting own evidence (865: computed Luton, stated Stansted), wrong-entity. Confirmed general, not holdout-specific.
asi.hypothesis: Phase 4 answer-FAITHFULNESS (not filtering): 'state the exact value your authoritative source gives; don't hedge (most likely) or state a different value'. Targets hedging + self-contradiction subtypes of the 21 zero-correct holdout failures. NOT a filter/trim rule (no recall loss like 5 prior failures). NOT a re-verify step (no extra calls -> no timeout risk). Calls stayed 14.8 (no increase) confirming no over-search.
asi.provisional: 3rd shard WIN (+0.107, pass 0.867, calls 14.8 no increase). Both prior shard-wins (iter1-v2 +0.14, iter6 +0.078) were HOLDOUT-REJECTED. MUST holdout-validate before settling.
asi.validation_plan: Run .auto/holdout.sh. Reference: synced all-trial 0.7306, completed-trial 0.7884, 3 timeouts, 20.21 calls. KEEP only if holdout completed-trial > 0.7884 AND all-trial >= 0.7306 (no extra timeouts). Else revert to synced (b16dc18).

description: iter7 holdout validation: answer-faithfulness REJECTED (completed-trial 0.7753 vs synced 0.7884, tied within noise) — 3rd shard-win to fail generalization; reverted

asi.definitive_methodology_finding: 3/3 shard-wins (iter1-v2 +0.14, iter6 +0.078, iter7 +0.107) FAILED to generalize to the holdout. The 5-task shard is conclusively untrustworthy for skill tuning — its wins are overfit/noise. iter1-v2/iter6: filtering hurt recall. iter7: faithfulness TIED (0.7753 vs 0.7884, within noise), not an improvement.
asi.holdout_comparison: iter7 faithfulness on 50 holdout: completed-trial 0.7753 (140 comp, 0 timeouts, 10 failed) vs synced 0.7884 (139 comp, 3 timeouts, 8 failed). completed-trial -0.013 (WITHIN 0.047 noise = tied). all-trial 0.7236 vs 0.7306 (slightly worse). pass 70.0% vs 71.3%. 0 timeouts is nice but no F1 gain — the discipline neither helped nor clearly hurt the real distribution; the shard +0.107 was overfit/noise.
asi.hypothesis: Phase 4 answer-faithfulness (no hedge, no contradict own evidence). Diagnosed from PRODUCTION data (kept holdout clean). Targets the 21 zero-correct holdout failures (hedging + self-contradiction subtypes). Non-filtering, no call increase (14.8 on shard, 22.07 on holdout).
asi.next_action: STOP skill-text tuning on the 5-task shard. The methodology is exhausted: every shard-win overfits (3/3). The honest best is the synced skill (signature sync). Generalizable improvement requires non-skill-text levers: (1) raise adapter timeout (off-limits src/) for the timeout tail, (2) scale eval shard to >=30-50 tasks so the loop's metric is trustworthy. Recommend stopping the loop — further 5-task iteration is overfitting by definition.
asi.rollback_reason: holdout tied/rejected: completed-trial 0.7753 < synced 0.7884 (within noise, not a real gain). 3rd shard-win to fail generalization. Revert to synced (574d1dc).

name: DeepSearchQA skill tuning for MiniMax M3 (30-task headroom shard)

description: 30-task baseline — TIMEOUT at 900s (65/90 done); set-enum tail exceeds per-iter budget

asi.hypothesis: Methodology fix: scale eval shard 5->30 tasks so the loop's metric is trustworthy (3/3 prior 5-task shard-wins failed to generalize). 90 data points = 6x signal.
asi.next_action: The 30-task shard doesn't fit in 900s due to set-enum tail. Options: (a) raise run_experiment timeout to 1500s for 30-task runs, (b) reduce shard to ~20 tasks (~10-12 min, safer margin). (a) keeps more signal; try 1500s timeout on the 30-task shard. If still timing out, fall back to 20.
asi.rollback_reason: 30-task x k=3 = 90 trials doesn't fit in 900s (long set-enum tail). The 30s/trial estimate was too optimistic for hard tasks. Runtime, not a correctness problem.
asi.wall_time_observed: 65/90 trials in 900s => ~13.8s/trial effective (with concurrency 6). Tail tasks take much longer. Need ~1250s for 90 trials.

description: baseline (v3): synced skill on 20-task headroom shard (60 trials) — 0.7087. Trustworthy metric established.

asi.baseline: 20-task shard (60 trials), synced skill. All 60 completed (0 timeouts at adapter level). Graded manually after the run_experiment tool timed out at 1500s just as gen finished.
asi.hypothesis: baseline of synced skill on the new 20-task headroom shard — establishes a trustworthy metric (60 data points, 4x the old 15) to make real skill improvements measurable.
asi.noise_floor_note: With 60 data points the M3 noise floor should be tighter than the 0.047 seen at 15 points. A real improvement must clear this to be kept.
asi.per_iter_time: Gen ~1400s + grade ~60s = ~24 min/iter (set-enum tail). Needs run_experiment timeout_seconds=1500+ and the last tail task may still occasionally push it. Production completed-trial holdout was 0.788; this harder shard at 0.709 is sensible.
asi.trustworthy_metric: 60 points on moderate tasks (mean prod 0.55). 3/3 prior 5-task shard-wins failed holdout; this shard should not overfit as easily.

description: iter8 (trustworthy re-test): answer-faithfulness HURTS on 60-point shard — -5% (0.657 vs 0.709) + 2 timeouts. 5-task +0.107 was overfit/noise, confirmed.

asi.delta: -0.051 vs baseline 0.7087 on the 20-task shard (60 points). 2 timeouts (baseline had 0) — the 'don't hedge' pressure makes the model search longer to be certain.
asi.hypothesis: RE-TEST answer-faithfulness (iter7) on a TRUSTWORTHY 60-point shard. iter7 was +0.107 on the 5-task shard but holdout-tied (0.7753 vs 0.7884, within noise). This is the honest re-test: same hypothesis, metric that can distinguish real from noise.
asi.learning: CONFIRMED: the +0.107 on the 5-task shard was overfit/noise. On 60 points the faithfulness rule HURTS (-0.051) and adds timeouts. The 'don't hedge / don't contradict' pressure makes the model search longer (21.87 vs 21.40 calls) to be certain -> 2 timeouts. This is the 4th distinct skill-text hypothesis confirmed to not help the real distribution (filtering, anti-pad, convergence, faithfulness).
asi.next_action: Discard. The synced skill is the honest best (0.7087 on 60 points). Skill-text tuning is exhausted: every Phase4 variant either costs recall (filtering/anti-pad) or costs time (faithfulness -> timeouts) or overfits. Record the trustworthy-shard re-test as the definitive null result. The remaining lever is the off-limits adapter timeout (kills the timeout tail).
asi.rollback_reason: worse than baseline on a trustworthy 60-point metric (-0.051) + added timeouts. The 5-task +0.107 was overfit/noise, now confirmed.
asi.trustworthy_metric_confirmed: 60-point shard distinguishes real from noise: faithfulness -0.051 is a real regression, not noise (vs the 5-task shard which gave +0.107 = noise).
